description: Every hazard `String.prototype.localeCompare` has past its declared types is ECMA-402's, and ECMA-262 hands that document the two positions it names `reserved1` and `reserved2`. So the entry is clean given both get nothing, and the call site decides: comparing two strings is green, an explicit `undefined` for the locale is green too, and a locale or an options bag floors the position that carries it. `spelled` is the boundary of that reading and why it is narrow — ECMA-262 writes no algorithm for `Number.prototype.toLocaleString`, so there are no steps to have read there and its silence is not evidence. It floors, and a change that colored it green off the same rule would be reading absence of a corpus as absence of a throw.
